title: Calcium, magnesium and phosphate
subtitle: Corrected calcium, arrhythmia risk and refeeding patterns
summary: Corrected calcium, arrhythmia risk and refeeding patterns
introduction: Use the reporting laboratory range. Corrected calcium formulas are approximations and become unreliable in critical illness, major acid–base disturbance, severe hypoalbuminaemia and renal failure; ionised calcium is preferable in these settings.

rows.name: Hypocalcaemia
notes: Consider vitamin D deficiency, hypoparathyroidism, renal failure, pancreatitis, sepsis, low magnesium or massive transfusion. Symptoms include perioral tingling, carpopedal spasm, tetany, seizure and prolonged QT.

rows.name: Hypercalcaemia
rows.referenceRange: Typical corrected calcium >2.60 mmol/L; ≥3.0 mmol/L is marked
notes: Consider malignancy, primary hyperparathyroidism, medication or granulomatous disease. Look for dehydration, constipation, vomiting, polyuria, confusion, weakness and shortened QT.

rows.name: Magnesium
notes: Low magnesium can cause tremor, weakness, seizures, hypokalaemia that is difficult to correct and ventricular arrhythmias including torsades. High magnesium can cause hyporeflexia, bradycardia, hypotension and respiratory depression.

rows.name: Phosphate
notes: Low phosphate can cause weakness, respiratory muscle failure, rhabdomyolysis and haemolysis. A rapid fall after nutrition in a malnourished patient suggests refeeding syndrome, often with low potassium and magnesium.

calculations.title: Approximate corrected calcium
interpretation: They become unreliable in critical illness, major acid–base disturbance, severe hypoalbuminaemia and renal failure; ionised calcium is preferable in these settings.

parityCases.description: Albumin 40 g/L leaves measured calcium unchanged.

urgentFindings: Tetany, seizure, stridor, prolonged QT or arrhythmia with suspected hypocalcaemia.
Corrected calcium around ≥3.0 mmol/L with dehydration, vomiting, confusion, weakness or ECG change.
Severe hypomagnesaemia with ventricular arrhythmia, seizure or persistent hypokalaemia.
Low phosphate with respiratory weakness, profound generalised weakness, rhabdomyolysis or suspected refeeding syndrome.
overrides: Use the reporting laboratory’s reference ranges and compare with previous results, symptoms, observations, medication and fluid status.
